name: AFGHANISTAN

flag.title: Afghan flag
flag.note: Black, red & green with white emblem

lead: Afghanistan sits at the crossroads of Asia, where mountains meet vast desert plains. The Hindu Kush range cuts through the middle like a spine of ice and rock. For thousands of years, Silk Road traders passed through Kabul, a great meeting point of ideas.
geo: Afghanistan has no sea coast. The Hindu Kush mountains cross the middle, with peaks above 7,000 m. The south is a hot, sandy desert called the Registan.
The Amu Darya river forms the northern border. The Wakhan Corridor, a thin finger of land, stretches east to touch China. In spring, wildflowers cover the valleys.
animals: The snow leopard prowls the high rocky passes. Its huge paws work like snowshoes. Marco Polo sheep, with giant curling horns, live above 4,000 m.
The Afghan hound is one of the oldest dog breeds. Its silky long fur kept it warm on mountain hunts. Ibex roam the valleys while golden eagles circle above.
culture: Afghans knot carpets by hand. One takes months and tells a story in colourful patterns. The poet Rumi, born near Balkh, is still read worldwide.
Every guest gets green tea with cardamom as a welcome. In buzkashi, the national sport, riders on horseback race to carry a goat carcass over a goal line.
history: Great empires crossed Afghanistan. Alexander the Great, the Mauryans, Genghis Khan's Mongols, and Timur all swept through. Each left traces in art, language, and culture.
In the 1800s, Britain and Russia played the 'Great Game' to control the region. Afghanistan kept its independence. The Soviet invasion in 1979 led to decades of turbulent rebuilding.
wows: Kandahar pomegranates are among the world's sweetest, prized for over 1,000 years.
Balkh, called 'Mother of Cities', is over 3,000 years old.
The Bamiyan Buddhas, carved 1,500 years ago, were once the tallest standing Buddhas.
Natural travertine dams make the Band-e Amir lakes vivid blue.
Buzkashi has been played here for over 1,000 years.
The 65 m Minaret of Jam is a UNESCO site in a remote valley.
Afghanistan borders six countries: Pakistan, Iran, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, and China.

myths.fact: Most Afghans are not Arabs. The biggest groups are Pashtuns, Tajiks, Hazaras, and Uzbeks.

myths.myth: Blue lapis stones come only from Egypt
myths.fact: Afghan mines have dug lapis lazuli for about 6,000 years. Ancient Egypt traded for it.
